destination.question: What determines the limits of gravitational effective descriptions, and when can their characteristic scales be separated from particle thresholds or the four-dimensional Planck scale?
destination.summary: Species arguments, discrete quantum numbers, several towers and proposed low-scale constructions ask different questions about scale separation. Their scales and assumptions must remain distinguishable.

systems: Particle towers and massive spin-2 fields
assumptions: A large periodic quantum number need not mean N particle species
Different towers can have different gaps and degeneracies
conventions: Do not identify a cancelling-fermion threshold, perturbative cutoff, species scale and quantum-gravity scale
A scenario allowing scale separation does not establish a universal bound
includes: Early constructions and later consistency proposals
excludes: A universal solution to the electroweak hierarchy

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a massive Abelian vector remain parametrically lighter than the completion of its anomalous infrared spectrum? The paper distinguishes the cancelling-fermion threshold, the further perturbative cutoff, and the quantum gravity scale.

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Match a local counterterm's gauge variation to the fermion-measure anomaly. The construction restores perturbative gauge invariance while exposing nonrenormalizability and the singular fixed-anomaly massless-vector limit.

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Sum many-body transition probabilities from one normalized incoming partial wave. Goldstone equivalence isolates longitudinal production, while factorial phase space determines which multiplicities constrain perturbation theory most strongly.

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Build symmetry-invariant operators and distinguish fixed mass coefficients from unknown derivative coefficients. This isolates a universal mass-induced cutoff and shows why removing the fermion mass alone need not decouple every irrelevant interaction.

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Restore Abelian gauge redundancy with a shifting scalar. In the Higgs reference construction, increase the vacuum expectation value and decrease the Higgs charge at fixed vector mass to decouple the radial field.

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Estimate the heavy-fermion contribution to the photon two-point function and compare its induced mass with mγ. A graviton analogue supplies the mixed-anomaly argument.

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Expand the Higgs theory around its vacuum and integrate out the radial fluctuation. This explicit matching example separates unavoidable mass dressing from radial-mass-dependent derivative corrections.

sources.title: A Spin‐2 Conjecture on the Swampland

evidence.text: The paper asks whether quantum gravity imposes a tower threshold on a fundamental massive spin-2 field, beyond the requirements of infrared consistency. The associated massless limit would otherwise produce an additional massless spin-2 field.

sources.title: The Quantum Gravity Scale and the Swampland

evidence.text: What scale controls the breakdown of semiclassical Einstein gravity, and how do its moduli dependence, emergent kinetic terms and infinite-distance behavior constrain gravitational effective theories?

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can infrared properties of scalar fields and particle towers identify gravitational EFTs compatible with quantum gravity? A separate unresolved issue is whether quantum gravity itself guarantees moduli and towers becoming massless in large-moduli limits.

sources.title: The dark dimension and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can the small observed vacuum-energy density identify an asymptotic quantum-gravity regime and thereby correlate infrared particle scales, extra-dimensional geometry, and the ultraviolet cutoff?

sources.title: Gravity Cutoff in Theories with Large Discrete Symmetries

evidence.text: Does an exact quantum number of large periodicity N require a gravitational cutoff below MP even without N particle species, and under what assumptions could this protect the weak scale?

sources.title: Continuum effective field theories, gravity, and holography

evidence.text: When can an EFT with a free or nearly-free continuum consistently include gravity, and how do holographic gapped-continuum realizations modify the Newtonian potential and the brane Friedmann equation?

sources.title: Scales of gravity

evidence.text: Can the quantum-gravity scale M* lie far below the particle-theory cutoff MSM, potentially near 10^(−3) eV, while observed gravity stays weak and an exponentially large tower of bulk states remains compatible with the observations considered?

sources.title: IR/UV mixing, towers of species and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Does quantum gravity constrain the independent choice of EFT infrared and ultraviolet cutoffs, and which mass scale characterizes the resulting light spectrum when several towers have different gaps and degeneracies?

sources.title: Phenomenology of low quantum gravity scale models

evidence.text: How can quantum gravity lie far below the four-dimensional Planck scale while accommodating gauge unification, supersymmetry breaking and phenomenology, and which fundamental scales appear motivated?

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Can a large number of quantum-field species force gravity to be weak relative to their mass scale, thereby explaining the weak–Planck hierarchy and the Higgs mass's sensitivity to a much larger cutoff?

sources.title: Lectures on the Swampland Program in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Could restrictions on EFT parameter space from quantum gravity change naturalness reasoning for the cosmological constant and electroweak hierarchy? The authors suggest UV/IR mixing as a possible connection, motivated by low-energy gravity and weak gauge coupling.

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: What restrictions does quantum gravity impose on continuous parameters and asymptotic scalar-field geometry? The imported conjectures connect scalar expectation values, infinite moduli-space diameter, and towers becoming exponentially light with geodesic distance.

destination.title: Distances, light towers and geometric limits
destination.question: Which scalar or geometric limits require a changed effective description, and under what assumptions do towers and field-space distances diagnose that change?
destination.summary: Separate the existence of moduli and towers from conditional explanations of exponential scaling. Large radius, finite excursions and comparisons across dimensions require different interpretations.

assumptions: The emergence calculation assumes a light tower, suitable spectral behavior and a common scalar-gravity strong-coupling scale
A tower-mass proxy for changing dimension is not a supplied kinetic metric for dimension
conventions: Path length need not equal endpoint geodesic distance
New low-energy modes can already belong to the higher-dimensional theory
Near-cutoff turnover does not guarantee that initially ultraviolet modes become very light
includes: Conditional derivations and unresolved foundational premises
excludes: A proof that every quantum gravity has moduli or the assumed towers

evidence.text: For strong curvature, the authors rewrite the metric and scalar using H1 and H2 and analyze the trace of Einstein's equation. Restricting these functions to Laplacian eigenfunctions leads to logarithmic behavior near relevant poles.

sources.title: Swampland, Gradient Flow and Infinite Distance

evidence.text: Construct entropy functionals for a generalized gradient flow and use them to define related field-space distances. This is the authors' reported construction; the supplied conclusion does not provide enough operations to reproduce it.

sources.title: The Convex Hull Swampland Distance Conjecture and Bounds on Non-geodesics

evidence.text: Substitute the heavy-field valley embedding into the parent kinetic metric. The resulting pullback metric measures the low-energy distance, including heavy-field backreaction along the valley.

sources.title: Super-Planckian Spatial Field Variations and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: The decomposition g(r)=γ(r)√ρ(r)=γ(r)γ̃(r)/r separates coupling-to-energy tracking from departures of the scalar profile from logarithmic behavior. Equations of motion near the free-field radius estimate the permitted growth of γ.

sources.title: Super-Planckian Spatial Field Variations and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Newtonian-potential bounds constrain scalar-gradient energy. Power-law profile families approach logarithmic radial behavior at large field variation; a maximal-variation argument also favors logarithmic profiles at fixed gravitational potential.
